author: Kylie Sczepanski
title: Judge gives homeless encampment another 90 days - NewsBreak
text:
By Kylie Sczepanski ,
4 hours ago
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — A judge is allowing the residents of the “Fallen Angels” homeless encampment near Dietrich Park to stay another 90 days as the city works to find them housing.
30th Circuit Court Judge Rosemarie Aquilina originally ordered the camp to be cleared by Nov. 14th, 90 days from when the case first started, under the condition the city found housing for all the camps residents.
Anthony Vincent, one of the camp’s residents, said there are the same number of people living there as there were a few months ago, and that while they are all on the necessary lists to find housing, only one person has received a voucher so far.
“We’re all just waiting to get into housing we’re all on the list we’ve all done what we’re supposed to do so like I said it’s just hurry up and wait game now,” Vincent said.
Mike Gorishek is the board president of Punks with Lunch. He said the camp’s inhabitants are battling the cold, and with a ban on propane and open flames, they’re running out of options.
“The number one need right now for this camp is [a] heat source,” he said. “The judge has banned the use of propane and open flame and those are some of the main heat sources here so the folks can survive the winter.”
The city’s attorney said they’re doing everything in their power to comply with the judge’s orders, but also say it’s getting harder as the days get colder and the shelters are at capacity.
Vincent disagrees and argues the city doesn’t care about them.
“What he wants to do is harm us and get us out of here put us right back out on the streets he doesn’t care if we live or die,” he said.
Aquilina says the court hearings will continue each Wednesday at 1 p.m. until the camp is cleared for good.
6 News has reached out to the city of Lansing for a reaction to the new deadline and camp resident’s concerns. A spokesperson says they can’t comment on cases that are ongoing.
